messages:
li (acme-corp): hey team, our embeddings throughput just tanked 5x this morning. tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec dropped from ~12k/s to ~2.4k/s. this started around 08:00 UTC. our app is timing out on search.

maria (support): sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal request + response (headers/metadata) and the project/model you hit?

li (acme-corp): sending example. note the response meta 'dim' seems off.
```
POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
Content-Type: application/json
{ "model": "embed-v1-large", "input": ["foo bar"], "project":"acme-prod" }
```
response: 
```
{ "data": [{ "embedding": [...], "meta": { "model":"embed-v1-large@v3", "dim": 128 } }], "usage": { "vectors":1 } }
```
expected dim is 1536 for embed-v1-large — seeing 128 looks like a small-embed fallback.

maria (support): that dim mismatch is suspicious. are you seeing any 4xx/5xx errors or auth/billing noise?

li (acme-corp): no errors, just slow. no billing alerts. token generation endpoints (text) are fine. only embeddings pipeline affected.

oncall-bot: Alert: embeddings-rate-regression detected for project acme-prod — vectors/sec below threshold for 10m. Incident created: INC-2028-452.

josh (eng-runtime): pinging infra. two immediate hypotheses: 1) routing sent traffic to a small-embed model variant (dim=128) which forces different batching/CPU path; 2) a quantization/kernel fallback made runtime drop to slow path. can you share a sample request_id from logs?

li (acme-corp): sample request id: req_202803_9f2b. sent to support DM.

sam (ml-eng): I pulled the logs for req_202803_9f2b. runtime shows: 
```
[08:02:18] routing: resolved model alias embed-v1-large -> embed-v1-small@v2 (policy: cost-fallback)
[08:02:18] batcher: accepting batch size=1 seq_len=64
[08:02:18] runtime: fallback to cpu-copy-embedding-path (quant table missing)
[08:02:19] gpu: kv cache hits ok, compute idle ~35%, queue depth 120
```
that routing line is the smoking gun — alias resolved to small variant. queue depth high because small variant processes fewer vectors per GPU batch causing higher request concurrency and less efficient kernels.

josh (eng-runtime): checking recent config push to variant-aliases. there was a deployment at 07:58 UTC that updated alias mappings for cost experiments. it looks like a mistaken mapping for the large alias pointed to the small model for "acme-prod" tier. rollback in progress.

maria (support): nice catch. immediate mitigation for customer: 1) pin request to explicit model version (embed-v1-large@v3) in their payload; 2) we can route their project to previous variant via temporary override. which do you prefer?

li (acme-corp): we can't change all callers quickly — please push override. pinning is fine as short term.

josh (eng-runtime): override applied at 08:06:12 UTC: embed-v1-large alias now points to embed-v1-large@v3 for acme-prod. we're seeing vectors/sec climb back toward baseline.

oncall-bot: Change applied by josh — alias-override(acme-prod):embed-v1-large -> embed-v1-large@v3.

sam (ml-eng): follow-up notes: root cause = faulty rollout of cost-experiment alias mapping that unintentionally included a high-traffic customer and pointed to a lower-dim variant. secondary impact = runtime took different execution path (no optimized kernels/quant tables) which increased per-vector latency and raised queue depth.

maria (support): li — can you confirm service quality? any remaining errors or latency?

li (acme-corp): confirmed: vectors/sec is back to ~11.5k/s and search latency normalized. huge thanks. can you send repro steps/what to watch so our SREs can verify on their side?

josh (eng-runtime): repro checklist for your SREs:
- call embeddings with model alias (embed-v1-large) and note response meta.dim. should be 1536.
- call with explicit pinned model (embed-v1-large@v3) to confirm behavior.
- check request headers for x-request-id and compare to runtime logs.
- run `GET /v1/aliases?project=acme-prod` to inspect alias mappings.
- if you see dim=128 unexpectedly, run `redwoodctl routing get --project acme-prod` (internal) or ask support.

sam (ml-eng): ops follow-ups for our team: add alias rollout guardrails (block if alias change affects top X customers), add quick-detect alert for dim drift (monitor model metadata returned by embeddings), and ensure quantization table presence is checked before variant becomes live.

maria (support): I'll summarize and close the incident once we have postmortem notes. will follow up with a private link to the rollback audit and the timeline. :thumbsup:

li (acme-corp): thanks all. appreciated the fast response. :pray:
